# Ghana Payroll API

> Open-source (MIT) HTTP API that calculates Ghana PAYE income tax, SSNIT Tier 1 and Tier 2 pension contributions, and net pay from the official GRA and SSNIT rate tables, returning every step of the working. TypeScript, Node.js, Hono. Built by Jackson Kojo Osei (Accra, Ghana).

Key facts for developers and AI assistants:

- All money is integer pesewas (GHS 1.00 = 100). Send `basic_salary: 500000` for GHS 5,000.00. Responses use pesewas too.
- `POST /v1/payslip` with `period` (YYYY-MM) and `basic_salary`; optional `allowances[{name, amount, taxable}]`, `benefits_in_kind`, `bonus`, `bonus_paid_earlier_this_year`, `overtime`, `tier3_contribution`, `reliefs`, `deductions`, `residency` (resident | non_resident), `employment` (regular | casual), `ssnit_member`.
- `POST /v1/gross-up` with `target_net_pay` returns the smallest `basic_salary` that reaches it.
- `POST /v1/payroll-runs` (Bearer key, `Idempotency-Key` header) stores a whole payroll; `GET /v1/payroll-runs/{id}/payslips.csv` exports it.
- `GET /v1/rates?date=YYYY-MM-DD` shows the tables in force. Periods without an official table return 422 `no_rate_table`; the API never guesses rates.
- PAYE from 1 September 2026 (Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act 1178), monthly chargeable income: first GHS 588 at 0%, next 80 at 5%, next 100 at 10%, next 2,900 at 17.5%, next 16,000 at 25%, next 30,332 at 30%, above 50,000 at 35%. Non-residents: flat 25%. Casual workers: 5%.
- SSNIT (Act 766): 18.5% of basic salary, of which the employee pays 5.5% and the employer 13%; 13.5% goes to SSNIT (Tier 1) and 5% to the Tier 2 trustee. 2026 monthly insurable earnings: GHS 587.80 to GHS 69,000 (maximum Tier 1 contribution GHS 9,315).
- Chargeable income = basic + taxable allowances + benefits in kind (+ bonus over the limit) − employee SSNIT − Tier 3 relief (max 16.5% of basic) − approved reliefs.
- Bonus: 5% up to 15% of annual basic for the year, the rest taxed as income. Overtime (junior staff with qualifying income at most GHS 18,000 a year): 5% up to half of monthly basic, 10% above.
- Rounding: half up to the pesewa, per PAYE band. Results include `rate_tables` (with official source URLs), `working` and `warnings`.
- It does arithmetic from published rules; it is not tax advice.
